page: Alibaba Cloud ecs.c6e.large is a compute-optimized virtual server instance powered by KVM virtualization. It is built on the x86_64 architecture and runs on an Intel Xeon 8269CY processor clocked at 2.5 GHz. The instance configuration provides 2 vCPUs derived from a single physical core using two hardware threads, paired with 4.0 GB of memory (2.0 GB per vCPU). CPU cache resources include 32 KB of L1 data cache, 1.0 MB of L2 cache, and a 35 MB L3 cache. Instruction set extensions include AVX, AVX-512F, and AVX-512 VNNI, alongside hardware AES support.

In hardware provisioning, the instance does not include bundled local storage or dedicated GPU acceleration, relying entirely on network-attached block storage for persistent data. Baseline networking throughput is rated at 1 Gbps, and no complimentary public IPv4 addresses are assigned by default.

Benchmark measurements position the ecs.c6e.large toward entry-level compute throughput due to its single physical core constraint. Single-core compute evaluations yielded a stress-ng score of 1305.19 and a Geekbench single-core score of 1156.0, both placing in the bottom 25%. Multi-core scores reached 1737.28 in stress-ng and 1379.0 in Geekbench, ranking in the bottom 10%. Memory read-only bandwidth registered 12.97 GB/sec and write bandwidth reached 11.91 GB/sec on large 256 MB blocks. Application metrics show Redis SET throughput of 1.7 million operations per second and static web serving throughput of 2.0 GB/sec, reflecting the constrained parallel capacity of the dual-thread core.

Given its 1:2 vCPU-to-memory ratio, ecs.c6e.large offers a low resource footprint suitable for lightweight compute tasks, small-scale web serving, proxy routing, and low-volume background workers. Workloads requiring sustained multi-threaded performance, high memory arrays, or local IOPS will require larger instances in the family.
